title: Nilpotent action and the specified principal Koszul completion unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$. Assume countable products of $R$-module sheaves are exact and use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a strict inverse sequence $X$, use the Roos complex $\mathsf R(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_jX_j\to\prod_jX_j)[-1]$ [def-weil-strict-roos-model], in reordered coordinates $(v,u)$ with differential $(dv,-du-(1-s)v)$. For $j\geq1$ put $L_j=[R\xrightarrow{t^j}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, with transitions $(t,1)$ [def-pur-principal-koszul-quotient-towers], and use right total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

For every unbounded complex $Q$ there is a natural short exact sequence of complexes of strict towers
$$0\to\operatorname{const}(Q)\xrightarrow{i}(Q\otimes_RL_j)_j\to Z(Q)\to0,$$
where $i_j(x)=(x,0)$, each $Z(Q)_j=Q[1]$, and its transitions are $t$. In degree $k$, $(Q\otimes L_j)^k=Q^k\oplus Q^{k+1}$ has differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx+(-1)^{k+1}t^jy,dy)$, and the quotient map to $Q[1]^k$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(-1)^ky$. If $t^rQ^k=0$ for every $k$ for some $r\geq1$, then $R\!\lim_j Z(Q)_j=0$ and the specific chain map
$$u_Q:Q\longrightarrow\mathsf R_j(Q\otimes_RL_j),\qquad x\longmapsto((i_jx)_j,0),$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. Here the total derived inverse limit of strict towers is that of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The maps $u_Q$ form a natural transformation on all complexes and all $R$-linear chain maps, independent of the choice of $r$. Thus for any strict tower $Q_n$ on which powers $t^{r_n}$ vanish termwise, they form a strict map of $n$-towers which is a quasi-isomorphism at each level, without a common exponent or any cohomological bound.

proof.text: Use the signed right-tensor coordinate theorem to obtain Z, level isomorphisms, i, p, hi and chi, with the canonical inverse coordinates, strict short exact sequence, signed differential, and transitions. These are constructed without any nilpotence hypothesis.

Evaluate i at every tower level and apply the explicit zero-homotopy Roos augmentation. This defines u on every complex. For a chain map b the naturality of i identifies b followed by every target level inclusion with the source inclusion followed by the tower map. The Roos map acts diagonally on both product coordinates. Product extensionality and the coordinate isomorphisms prove the naturality equality for u. The augmentation formula gives its required (0,Pi.lift i) coordinates.

Fix an exponent a>=1 annihilating every term of Q. Induction on a proves that the a-th endomorphism power of scalar multiplication acts on a section x by t^a x, so this power is the zero sheaf morphism. Let e_n identify Z(Q)_n^k with Q^(k+1). Induction on b, using the quotient transition identity, gives s^b pi_n e_n = pi_(n+b) e_(n+b) t^b for the product shift s. For b=a this is zero. Cancel e_n and use product extensionality to obtain s^a=0 in every degree.

The module-sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian after passage to its equivalent coefficient-universe small site, as in the existing total derived-limit construction. Apply the generic Roos nilpotent exact-augmentation lemma to the short exact sequence and the product-shift nilpotence just proved. It gives QuasiIso(u_Q) and vanishing of RF(Q Z(Q)) for every total right derived limit RF with unit eta.

For an arbitrary outer strict tower, whisker the natural transformation u with the tower functor. At level n apply the preceding argument with a_n, using only the annihilation hypothesis at that level. This gives every required quasi-isomorphism with no common exponent or cohomological bound.
